Today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 candidate version contains a short clip that appears to demonstrate the 'Visual Intelligence' feature of Apple's rumored camera-equipped AirPods. Please watch the following video.

macOS 26.7 contains a demonstration clip of camera-equipped AirPods

MacRumors discovered a short clip included in today's macOS Tahoe 26.7 candidate version, in which a man wearing AirPods appears to ask Siri to remember a book he is looking at. Siri's voiceover says:

The camera itself cannot be seen in the clip, and the earbuds look very similar to the existing AirPods Pro. The most obvious difference is the stem, which looks slightly thicker.

Aaron Perris has also posted the same clip to X:

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman previously reported that Apple may launch camera-equipped AirPods as early as this year under the codename B790. Earlier, MacRumors also found references to B790 in the macOS 26.7 candidate version, including a code string for an 'image stream'.

It is worth noting that, according to reports, these AirPods are separate from another camera-equipped model Apple has been developing under the codename B798, as previously reported by Bloomberg, which is not expected to launch until 2027.

Given Apple's decision to include this demonstration clip in the macOS 26.7 candidate version, these camera-equipped AirPods are very likely to be officially announced at next month's iPhone event.

What are your thoughts on this clip? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
